newsitem.title: UK: Lonrho reopens bidding for hotels - paper.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho reopens bidding for hotels - paper.

text.p: Conglomerate Lonrho Plc has cancelled a deal that gave Saudi investor Prince al-Waleed bin Talal exclusive negotiating rights in his bid to buy the company's Princess chain of luxury hotels, said the British Observer newspaper.
According to insiders it withdrew his preferred bidder status a "few weeks ago", because it was frustrated by delays, the newspaper said.
A spokesman for Lonrho said there had always been several parties interested but refused to comment on any particular approach.

Lonrho expected to announce the sale of the 10-strong hotel chain in November to the Prince for a price estimated by analysts at 350 million pounds ($567.4 million). The sale of the hotels forms part of Lonrho's plan to focus on its mining interests.
Lonrho has recently been approached by other hotel companies including Marriott International, said the paper, and informal talks are believed to be underway.
The prince, a nephew of King Fahd, recently paid 104 million pounds for the luxurious George V hotel in Paris and his other business interests include Canary Wharf in London and Disneyland in Paris.
